findings.F1: In the choppy profile, a larger 30-day fall is followed by a larger 7-day fall: the slope of the 7-day unusual move on the 30-day return, in standard units, is 0.145 (t 2.04, 111 cases on 54 days). After 30-day rises the slope is -0.004 (t -0.04, 104 cases on 48 days). This is the tested idea's own falls-only effect. It is not a new pattern, and the brief's claim that the effect is symmetric does not hold.
findings.F2: Outside the choppy profile, the 30-day return does not order the next 7 days (slope -0.009, t -0.15, 1004 cases on 154 days). The 60-day return does not order them in the choppy profile either (slope 0.038, t 0.60, 135 cases). The month effect is confined to the brief's own situation.
findings.F3: Inside the choppy profile, the 30-day slope is not steady from year to year. It is -0.16 in 2018 (t -0.81), 0.07 in 2019 (t 0.88), 0.52 in 2020 (t 2.26) and 0.28 in 2021 (t 2.38). No window with at least 7 case days reaches t 1.5 (w18: 0.29, t 1.40).
findings.F4: The book's largest days come from big moves against the coin, not from a separate pattern. On the 62 best coin-days the book made +6.8 % while the coin fell 11.8 %. On the 62 worst it lost 6.5 % while the coin rose 15.1 %. Its losses are short squeezes.

no_ideas: The only effect that stands out is the tested idea's own falls-only continuation in a choppy market (F1, F2), which is already being tested. Across 30-day, 60-day, 14-day, 7-day and 1-day returns, range, volatility, weekday, year, window, trade length and the book's extreme days, no other pattern clears chance given how many angles were examined (F3 to F6).
